summary: A lookout site since the 1920s, rebuilt three times before the current 1965 R-6 flattop; staffed into the 1970s and now a drive-up rental.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab with wraparound catwalk on 41-foot timber tower

access.note: Forest Service rental cabin, drive-up via well-maintained gravel road; entry by combination lock obtained from ranger district before arrival

visit.trail_note: Reachable by car via gravel road; nearby hiking along Deer Ridge and Ruby Ridge

events.note: First lookout structure at Deer Ridge was a cupola cabin, built in the 1920s
L-4 cab built on a 20-foot pole tower
L-4 cab built on a 40-foot timber tower
Current 41-foot R-6 flattop cab with catwalk built
Earliest named staff on record: William Kuntz
Last staffing on record: Paula Stueve and Kim Norwood, late season

evidence.supports: 41' R-6 flattop with catwalk built 1965, 15'x15', preceded by 1935 L-4/20' pole and 1949 L-4/40' timber tower, rental
evidence.quote: The Deer Ridge Lookout is a 41' tall 15'x15' R-6 flattop with catwalk built in 1965. It was preceded by an L-4 on a 20' pole tower (1935) and an L-4 on a 40' timber tower (1949).

evidence.supports: 40-foot timber frame, 14'x14' cabin with wraparound catwalk, drive-up gravel road, sleeps two with twin beds, no water, pit toilet 50 yards away, combination lock entry, children discouraged
evidence.quote: The 14' X 14' cabin has a wraparound catwalk, with a trap door that lifts for access to the tower's entrance staircase... A pit toilet is located 50 yards away.

evidence.supports: Drive-up access via well-maintained gravel road
evidence.quote: The lookout can be accessed by car and the gravel road to the lookout is well maintained.

evidence.supports: Views of Purcell mountains, Canada, Montana, Moyie River valley; 24 miles from Bonners Ferry
evidence.quote: Deer Ridge Lookout, perched on a 40 foot timber frame, boasts excellent views of the Purcell mountain ranges of Northern Idaho, Canada and Montana. Located 24 miles northeast of Bonners Ferry

evidence.supports: 1920s cupola cabin, 1935 pole L-4, 1949 40' pole L-4, 1965 current 41' TT Flat built; staffed 1933 through 1975
evidence.quote:
The first lookout at Deer Ridge was in the 1920s when a Cupola cabin was built.
1935 – Pole L-4 tower was built.
1949 – 40' pole L-4 was built.
1965 – Current 41' TT Flat was built.

evidence.supports: Last recorded staff, 1975, Paula Stueve and Kim Norwood, late season
evidence.quote:
1975
Paula Stueve (Forest Fire Lookout Page ; Bonners Ferry Herald - 08/14/75) — Late Season; Moved to new tower on Black Mountain in August
Kim Norwood (Bonners Ferry Herald - 08/14/75)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR states the 1965 cab is 15'x15'; Recreation.gov states the current cabin is 14'x14'. Both figures are given in the story rather than picking one.

sources.title: Deer Ridge Lookout, Idaho Panhandle National Forests

notes_for_editor: Idaho Fire Lookouts lists many more named seasonal staff (Odell, Black, Walters, Baker, Voll, etc.) between 1946 and 1972; only a sample is named in the story to keep it readable, with full list available in the source. Cabin footprint (15x15 vs 14x14) differs slightly between NHLR and Recreation.gov; both are given rather than resolved.
